_meta.purpose: OS six-inch writing-style -> feature-class ground truth for GB1900 Tier-1 typography typing.
_meta.source: OS 404 'Character of Writing for Ordnance Survey Plans' (June 1914), per-feature writing table (1/10560 & 6-inch column), pp.9-11; antiquities row p.9. See developer/plan-gb1900-typing.md sec 4.2.0.
_meta.usage: Tier-1: VLM emits os_style; look up expected feature classes here. A 'Stump' verdict = undifferentiated, defer to Tier-0 text.

style_legend.Stump: standard stamped hand; the DEFAULT for undifferentiated minor features

style_to_type_token._note: Coarse single feature-token per OS style, for the Tier-1 os_style->type step. RC/Ornamental = prominent settlement/admin; RP = named place/building; IC = water; EC/OldEnglish/GermanText = antiquity (by period); Stump = defer to Tier-0 text.

antiquities_by_period.note: Ancient localities: same as other antiquities by period, but with finer lines (OS 404 p.9).

case_size_hierarchy.note: Within caps styles, size + tracking split the settlement/admin hierarchy.
case_size_hierarchy.wide_spaced_caps: parish / boundary / administrative division / extended physical area

caveat: On the SIX-INCH, ~half of feature classes fall to 'Stump' (undifferentiated). Typography reliably separates only: prominent settlement/admin (RC/Ornamental/size), water (IC), antiquities by period (EC/OldEnglish/GermanText), named buildings (RP). The Stump mass must be typed from text (Tier 0).
